 "content": "# Continual-ARC note: diagonal-color pattern -> tiled output

Observed solved task `task-6dd33444` (test was 26x26): the sparse input contains diagonal colored traces; output is a full-grid periodic color weave. The output was generated by taking the short repeating color sequence and shifting its phase one position to the right on each successive row. Equivalently, for a cycle `S` of length `k`, output[r][c] = S[(c-r) mod k], tiled to the whole grid.

Evidence/examples:
- Demo 2 (24x24) used cycle `S=[3,5,9,7,5]`; rows were right-shifted cyclically, e.g. row0 `3,5,9,7,5,...`, row1 `5,3,5,9,7,...`.
- Solved test (26x26) used `S=[3,5,4,3]`; row0 `3,5,4,3,...`, row1 `3,3,5,4,...`, row2 `4,3,3,5,...`, row3 `5,4,3,3,...`.

Practical approach on future similar instances: infer the short color cycle from how the diagonal traces encode/repeat their colors, then fill every cell with the cycle using the diagonal phase formula above. Verify cycle length and order from visible trace structure; do not assume the colors are all distinct (the observed cycles repeat colors). Demo 1 was horizontal bands and transformed to repeated horizontal color runs, so inspect task geometry before applying the diagonal-shift formula blindly.
